title: MLX buffers: graph detachment does not end in-flight storage ownership
summary: Non-tracer graph references can detach after scheduling while backend-specific captures or temporaries retain buffers needed by queued work.

software: ml-explore/mlx at bff10220c742907f0c68e55ff174aaea56f74e3d; later revisions require reinspection
conditions: Actual backend, streams, shapes/dtypes and evaluation boundary are recorded.
CPU, Metal and CUDA source paths are distinguished; discovery or catalog placement is not runtime qualification.

claims.description: array::detach clears primitive, input and sibling graph references. eval_impl marks arrays evaluated and detaches non-tracers after primitive dispatch.

The CPU dispatch captures buffers and temporaries; Metal commit/completion callbacks capture buffers; CUDA retains non-donated inputs and siblings as encoder temporaries. Donation and tracer handling are explicit and backend-specific.

downstream_impact: An InferRSI transfer hypothesis for a matching MLX workload; no implicit vLLM, MLX-LM or other engine compatibility is claimed.
recommendations: Trace the selected backend retention owner and actual completion before interpreting dropped graph/Python references as storage reclamation.
validation_plan: On a separately authorized matching backend, retain checked outputs while releasing graph references, then distinguish in-flight retention from post-completion allocator caching.
limitations: This card establishes retention obligations, not allocator eviction, a universal reclamation threshold, zero-copy or memory savings.
Backend mechanisms are not interchangeable. No native lifetime, memory, model or service validation was run.
